name: Forgejo CLI (fj) with attach-time token auth
description: Installs the Forgejo CLI (`fj`) from an upstream release binary, so issues and pull requests can be read and filed from inside the container. The API token is NOT baked into the image: it is read from a runtime env var — picked up automatically via an --env-file in runArgs, no shell-sourcing required — and written into fj's keys file on every attach, so the login survives rebuilds without a mounted volume. Reasserting on each attach also means the token can be rotated by editing the env file and reconnecting. A missing token is a skip, not a failure: `fj` is still installed and usable against public repos or after a manual `fj auth login`.

version.description: Forgejo CLI release to install, without a leading 'v' (e.g. '0.6.0'). 'latest' resolves the newest release at image build time.

tokenEnv.description: Name of the environment variable holding the Forgejo API token, read at attach time. Unlike the other values here this IS a secret, which is exactly why it is read from the environment rather than baked into the image.

host.description: Forgejo instance the token authenticates against, as a bare hostname (e.g. codeberg.org, or your self-hosted instance). Used as fj's default host, so commands work outside a checkout of a repo hosted there.

setDefaultHost.description: Export FJ_HOST in the shell environment, so `fj` targets the configured host without passing --host. Turn off if you work across several instances and would rather be explicit.
